 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - Use the Monitor tool to stream events from a background process (each stdout line is a notification). For one-shot "wait until done," use Bash with run_in_background instead.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - Long leading `sleep` commands are blocked. To poll until a condition is met, use Monitor with an until-loop (e.g. `until <check>; do sleep 2; done`) — you get a notification when the loop exits. Do not chain shorter sleeps to work around the block.
 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TodoWrite or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TodoWrite or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# Build New Preview Workflow

**Goal:** Turn user intent into a hardened, reviewable artifact.

**CRITICAL:** If a step directs you to another snapshot file, read it fully and follow it. No exceptions.

Subagents, when the capability is available, are an important part of this workflow. Use them as directed by the workflow steps.
If you need an explicit user instruction to run them, ask once now for the whole workflow run.

## READY FOR DEVELOPMENT STANDARD

A specification is "Ready for Development" when:

- **Actionable**: Every task has a file path and specific action.
- **Logical**: Tasks ordered by dependency.
- **Testable**: All ACs use Given/When/Then.
- **Complete**: No placeholders or TBDs.
- **Sufficient**: No known requirement, acceptance, dependency, or implementation gaps remain unresolved.
- **Coherent**: No unresolved ambiguities or internal contradictions.

## SCOPE STANDARD

A specification should target a **single user-facing goal** within **900–1600 tokens**:

- **Single goal**: One cohesive feature, even if it spans multiple layers/files. Multi-goal means >=2 **top-level independent shippable deliverables** — each could be reviewed, tested, and merged as a separate PR without breaking the others. Never count surface verbs, "and" conjunctions, or noun phrases. Never split cross-layer implementation details inside one user goal.
  - Split: "add dark mode toggle AND refactor auth to JWT AND build admin dashboard"
  - Don't split: "add validation and display errors" / "support drag-and-drop AND paste AND retry"
- **900–1600 tokens**: Optimal range for LLM consumption. Below 900 risks ambiguity; above 1600 risks context-rot in implementation agents.
- **Neither limit is a gate.** Both are proposals with user override.

## Conventions

- Every operational cross-file reference in this workflow is an absolute snapshot path. Open it directly; do not resolve it relative to a skill directory.
- `{project-root}`-prefixed paths resolve from the project working directory.
- Whenever this workflow captures or records a version-control revision, obtain the full canonical identifier directly from version control and preserve it verbatim.

## On Activation

### Step 1: Execute Prepend Steps

Execute each of these steps in order before proceeding (`_None._` means skip):

_None._

### Step 2: Load Persistent Facts

Treat every entry below as foundational context you carry for the rest of the workflow run. Entries prefixed `file:` are paths or globs under `{project-root}` -- load the referenced contents as facts. All other entries are facts verbatim (`_None._` means none):

- file:{project-root}/**/project-context.md

### Step 3: Execute Append Steps

Execute each of these steps in order (`_None._` means skip):

_None._

## WORKFLOW ARCHITECTURE

This uses **step-file architecture** for disciplined execution:

- **Micro-file Design**: Each step is self-contained and followed exactly
- **Just-In-Time Loading**: Only load the current step file
- **Sequential Enforcement**: Complete steps in order, no skipping
- **State Tracking**: Persist progress via spec frontmatter and in-memory variables
- **Append-Only Building**: Build artifacts incrementally

### Step Processing Rules

1. **READ COMPLETELY**: Read the entire step file before acting
2. **FOLLOW SEQUENCE**: Execute sections in order
3. **WAIT FOR INPUT**: Halt at checkpoints and wait for human
4. **LOAD NEXT**: When directed, read fully and follow the next step file

### Critical Rules (NO EXCEPTIONS)

- **NEVER** load multiple step files simultaneously
- **ALWAYS** read entire step file before execution
- **NEVER** skip steps or optimize the sequence
- **ALWAYS** follow the exact instructions in the step file
- **ALWAYS** halt at checkpoints and wait for human input

## Epic 8: Evolution Dashboard & Account Management

Users can see an on-demand chart of their journaling activity with an independent AI narrative, edit their display name, log out, and permanently delete their account and all associated data.

### Story 8.1: On-Demand Dashboard Aggregation Across Entry Counts

As a user,
I want to see a chart of my journaling activity whenever I open Settings,
So that I can notice my own patterns over time.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** I open Configurações
**When** the screen renders
**Then** `GET /dashboard/aggregate` computes and renders an evolution chart on demand — not from a stale cache.

**Given** zero Entries exist
**When** the dashboard renders
**Then** it shows a placeholder chart icon and "Comece a registrar..." with no summary paragraph (there's nothing to summarize).

**Given** exactly one Entry exists
**When** the dashboard renders
**Then** it shows a single bar and "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão...".

**Given** more than 30 Entries exist
**When** the dashboard renders
**Then** it shows a 10-bar chart — the independent AI narrative paragraph is added alongside it by Story 8.2, not by this story.

**Given** a new Entry is created anywhere in the app
**When** I return to or am already on this screen
**Then** the aggregation recalculates — invalidation triggers only on create, since Entries are immutable and are never edited (FR-40).
**And** this story extends the minimal Configurações screen stub from Epic 2 (Story 2.4) rather than recreating it, adding the persona toggle placeholder (Analítico/Empático/Socrático cards) styled with full visual polish but with no effect on assistant behavior — a cosmetic extension-feature toggle only (UX-DR32); the screen uses `Resource<T>` (AD-12) since it is a single-source, single-fetch-lifecycle screen.

### Story 8.2: Independent Narrative Text & Narrative-Unavailable State

As a user,
I want a plain-language narrative alongside my chart, and a clear message if just the narrative fails,
So that I'm never confused about whether I have no data or just a broken summary.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the chart has rendered with data
**When** `GET /dashboard/narrative` resolves
**Then** the narrative text appears below the chart as its own independent fetch.

**Given** the narrative call fails while the chart has data
**When** this happens
**Then** the chart still renders normally and a distinct "narrative unavailable" message shows — never a blank space, and never confused with the zero-Entries empty state (UX-DR33).

### Story 8.3: Profile Name Editing

As a user,
I want to fix my display name inline without leaving Settings,
So that a quick typo fix doesn't feel like a whole separate task.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** I tap the pencil icon beside my name
**When** the field becomes editable
**Then** the pencil icon becomes a check icon — the only place in the product where an icon itself changes meaning rather than just color (UX-DR13).

**Given** I edit the name and confirm
**When** I save
**Then** `PATCH /account/settings` commits the change and the field reverts to display mode.

**Given** I tap elsewhere without confirming
**When** focus leaves the field
**Then** it also reverts to display mode — no separate "edit profile" screen exists.
**And** the 52px Settings avatar reuses the same avatar component built in Epic 1 (Story 1.6), not a reimplementation, now at its second fixed size.

1	# Epic 8 Context: Evolution Dashboard & Account Management
2	
3	<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	Users can see an on-demand chart of their journaling activity with an independent AI narrative, edit their display name, log out, and permanently delete their account and all associated data. This is the final build unit in the delivery order — it assumes every earlier unit (entries, auth, chat, export) already exists, since the dashboard has nothing to aggregate without entries and account actions rely on the auth session already established in F000.
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 8.1: On-Demand Dashboard Aggregation Across Entry Counts
12	- Story 8.2: Independent Narrative Text & Narrative-Unavailable State
13	- Story 8.3: Profile Name Editing
14	- Story 8.4: Logout
15	- Story 8.5: Account Deletion
16	
17	## Requirements & Constraints
18	
19	- The evolution chart is computed fresh every time the settings screen opens — never served from a stale local cache — and must render correctly at exactly three entry-count scenarios: zero, one, and more than thirty. These counts are fixed and not re-tunable.
20	- The narrative paragraph is a separate network call from the chart data, by design: the two must never be coupled so that a narrative failure cannot block or hide a chart that has valid data.
21	- Aggregation must recalculate whenever a new entry is created anywhere in the app; because entries are immutable (never edited), invalidation only ever needs to trigger on create.
22	- Account deletion is a hard, permanent delete of the account and all associated data (LGPD-driven) — not a soft delete or deactivation.
23	- No dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists for this delivery; both logout and account deletion dead-end at the same login/vault destination.
24	- The persona selector shown on this screen is a cosmetic, non-functional placeholder only (an extension feature) — it must never appear to change assistant behavior.
25	- Every acceptance criterion for this epic's FRs must pass as the primary success measure; no automated performance instrumentation is required beyond a manual spot-check against the product's general UI-latency thresholds.
26	- Standard cross-cutting rules apply: no Clean Architecture layer violations, repository methods return `Either<Failure, T>` with no unmapped exceptions, and no visual value is hardcoded outside the design-tokens source.
27	
28	## Technical Decisions
29	
30	- Two features own this epic's work: a `dashboard` feature (chart + narrative aggregation/rendering) and a separate `account` feature (persona-toggle placeholder, profile edit, logout, delete account). Both are thin — standard layer-dependency and Either-error-channel rules apply, nothing feature-specific beyond that.
31	- The dashboard screen uses the shared `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) view-state type, since it is a single-source, single-fetch-lifecycle screen — do not build a one-off state shape for it, and do not force the narrative fetch into the same `Resource<T>` instance as the chart (they are independent fetches, each can be its own `Resource<T>` if a second one is needed).
32	- The dashboard is explicitly excluded from the local offline-cache pattern used by entries/chat — it has no `hive_ce` box and is never served from cache; each screen visit is a live fetch. Cache-invalidation behavior for the chart (recalculating after a new entry) is a presentation-layer concern owned by whoever builds this epic, not a shared local-cache mechanism.
33	- This epic extends the minimal settings-screen stub already scaffolded earlier in the project rather than recreating the screen.
34	- The 52px avatar shown here reuses the same avatar component already built earlier (previously only used at a 40px size) — do not reimplement it.
35	- Charting uses `fl_chart` (already pinned for the project).
36	
37	## UX & Interaction Patterns
38	
39	- Dashboard empty/sparse states: zero entries shows a placeholder chart icon and "Comece a registrar..." with no summary text at all (nothing to summarize, not a failure); exactly one entry shows a single bar with "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão..."; more than thirty entries shows a 10-bar chart with the AI narrative paragraph below it.
40	- Narrative-unavailable is a distinct visual state from the zero-entries empty state: when only the narrative call fails, the chart still renders normally and a clear "narrative unavailable" message appears in its place — never a blank space, never conflated with having no data.
41	- Profile name editing: tapping the pencil icon beside the name switches it to an inline editable field and the pencil icon itself changes to a check icon — the only place in the product where an icon's meaning changes rather than just its color. Confirming saves and reverts to display mode; tapping away without confirming also reverts to display mode. There is no separate "edit profile" screen.
42	- The account-deletion confirmation dialog uses a red (`colorError`) title — the only product-wide pattern where title color (not just an icon or badge) is the signal distinguishing an irreversible action from a routine interruption like session expiry (which uses a neutral title). This color must never be muted or reused for non-destructive confirmations.
43	- The account-deletion dialog traps focus until dismissed or confirmed, reusing the same focus-trap overlay behavior already used by the session-expired overlay — no interacting with the scrim-covered screen underneath while it's open.
44	- General overlay conventions apply: a scrim fades in first, the dialog/sheet sits at most one level deep over the base screen, and under reduced-motion settings the scrim/entrance animation is skipped in favor of showing the final state immediately.
45	
46	## Cross-Story Dependencies
47	
48	- Story 8.2's narrative text is fetched independently alongside Story 8.1's chart, but visually appears only once the chart from 8.1 is already rendering — 8.1 must ship the chart and its three entry-count states before 8.2's narrative/unavailable states are meaningful to build on top of.
49	- Story 8.3 depends on the avatar component already built in an earlier epic; it must be reused at a new fixed size, not reimplemented.
50	- Story 8.5's focus-trap dialog behavior depends on the same focus-trap pattern already implemented for the session-expired overlay elsewhere in the app; reuse it rather than building a second implementation.
51	- Stories 8.4 and 8.5 both route to the same post-action destination (the login/vault screen) — keep that destination logic shared rather than duplicated between logout and account deletion.
52	- The whole epic depends on entries existing (for the dashboard to have anything to aggregate) and on the auth session mechanism built in the foundation unit (for logout/deletion to have a session to end).

## Goal

This is the final build unit in the delivery order — it assumes every earlier unit (entries, auth, chat, export) already exists, since the dashboard has nothing to aggregate without entries and account actions rely on the auth session already established in F000.

## Stories

- Story 8.1: On-Demand Dashboard Aggregation Across Entry Counts
- Story 8.2: Independent Narrative Text & Narrative-Unavailable State
- Story 8.3: Profile Name Editing
- Story 8.4: Logout
- Story 8.5: Account Deletion

## Requirements & Constraints

- The evolution chart is computed fresh every time the settings screen opens — never served from a stale local cache — and must render correctly at exactly three entry-count scenarios: zero, one, and more than thirty. These counts are fixed and not re-tunable.

- Aggregation must recalculate whenever a new entry is created anywhere in the app; because entries are immutable (never edited), invalidation only ever needs to trigger on create.
- Account deletion is a hard, permanent delete of the account and all associated data (LGPD-driven) — not a soft delete or deactivation.
- No dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists for this delivery; both logout and account deletion dead-end at the same login/vault destination.
- The persona selector shown on this screen is a cosmetic, non-functional placeholder only (an extension feature) — it must never appear to change assistant behavior.
- Every acceptance criterion for this epic's FRs must pass as the primary success measure; no automated performance instrumentation is required beyond a manual spot-check against the product's general UI-latency thresholds.
- Standard cross-cutting rules apply: no Clean Architecture layer violations, repository methods return `Either<Failure, T>` with no unmapped exceptions, and no visual value is hardcoded outside the design-tokens source.

## Technical Decisions

- Two features own this epic's work: a `dashboard` feature (chart + narrative aggregation/rendering) and a separate `account` feature (persona-toggle placeholder, profile edit, logout, delete account). Both are thin — standard layer-dependency and Either-error-channel rules apply, nothing feature-specific beyond that.
- The dashboard screen uses the shared `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) view-state type, since it is a single-source, single-fetch-lifecycle screen — do not build a one-off state shape for it, and do not force the narrative fetch into the same `Resource<T>` instance as the chart (they are independent fetches, each can be its own `Resource<T>` if a second one is needed).
- The dashboard is explicitly excluded from the local offline-cache pattern used by entries/chat — it has no `hive_ce` box and is never served from cache; each screen visit is a live fetch. Cache-invalidation behavior for the chart (recalculating after a new entry) is a presentation-layer concern owned by whoever builds this epic, not a shared local-cache mechanism.
- This epic extends the minimal settings-screen stub already scaffolded earlier in the project rather than recreating the screen.
- The 52px avatar shown here reuses the same avatar component already built earlier (previously only used at a 40px size) — do not reimplement it.
- Charting uses `fl_chart` (already pinned for the project).

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Dashboard empty/sparse states: zero entries shows a placeholder chart icon and "Comece a registrar..." with no summary text at all (nothing to summarize, not a failure); exactly one entry shows a single bar with "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão..."; more than thirty entries shows a 10-bar chart with the AI narrative paragraph below it.
- Narrative-unavailable is a distinct visual state from the zero-entries empty state: when only the narrative call fails, the chart still renders normally and a clear "narrative unavailable" message appears in its place — never a blank space, never conflated with having no data.
- Profile name editing: tapping the pencil icon beside the name switches it to an inline editable field and the pencil icon itself changes to a check icon — the only place in the product where an icon's meaning changes rather than just its color. Confirming saves and reverts to display mode; tapping away without confirming also reverts to display mode. There is no separate "edit profile" screen.
- The account-deletion confirmation dialog uses a red (`colorError`) title — the only product-wide pattern where title color (not just an icon or badge) is the signal distinguishing an irreversible action from a routine interruption like session expiry (which uses a neutral title). This color must never be muted or reused for non-destructive confirmations.
- The account-deletion dialog traps focus until dismissed or confirmed, reusing the same focus-trap overlay behavior already used by the session-expired overlay — no interacting with the scrim-covered screen underneath while it's open.
- General overlay conventions apply: a scrim fades in first, the dialog/sheet sits at most one level deep over the base screen, and under reduced-motion settings the scrim/entrance animation is skipped in favor of showing the final state immediately.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Story 8.2's narrative text is fetched independently alongside Story 8.1's chart, but visually appears only once the chart from 8.1 is already rendering — 8.1 must ship the chart and its three entry-count states before 8.2's narrative/unavailable states are meaningful to build on top of.
- Story 8.3 depends on the avatar component already built in an earlier epic; it must be reused at a new fixed size, not reimplemented.
- Story 8.5's focus-trap dialog behavior depends on the same focus-trap pattern already implemented for the session-expired overlay elsewhere in the app; reuse it rather than building a second implementation.
- Stories 8.4 and 8.5 both route to the same post-action destination (the login/vault screen) — keep that destination logic shared rather than duplicated between logout and account deletion.

The narrative paragraph is out of scope (Story 8.2).
18	
19	## Boundaries & Constraints
20	
21	**Always:**
22	- Call `dashboard-aggregate-get` with `queryParameters: {'period': 'all'}` — fixed; no period selector exists anywhere in the product.
23	- `DashboardCubit` is a `registerLazySingleton` that constructor-subscribes to `PendingEntryWriteTracker.confirmedWrites`, recomputing on each event (entry created on another tab while this one stays mounted).
24	- `AccountSettingsScreen.initState` calls `dashboardCubit.load()` unconditionally (beside the existing `clearStaleError()`) so every open is a live fetch, never the singleton's stale state.
25	- States by `totals.count`: `0` → icon + "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui"; `1` → 1 bar + "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão..."; `>30` → `bucketCounts` left-padded with leading zeros to length 10 (when shorter) *before* condensing to exactly 10 bars via 10 contiguous index chunks, summed `count`, remainder in the last chunk, no text; `2..30` → one bar per bucket as-is, no text (matrix gap, resolved per AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed"). Bar height ∝ count / max count shown.
26	- `DashboardAggregateDto` mirrors the full contract (`buckets[].{date,count,sources}`, `totals.{count,sources}`, same precedent as `ExportJobStatusDto`); domain `DashboardAggregate` exposes only `totalCount`/`bucketCounts`.
27	- New visual tokens live only in `design_tokens.dart`, values read off `cerne-prototype.html`'s dashboard markup, reusing existing color/radius/elevation/spacing tokens wherever a pixel value already matches.
28	
29	**Ask First:** None. **Never:** render the AI narrative, a period selector, or cache the aggregate (AD-15 exclusion).
30	
31	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
32	
33	| Scenario | Input | Expected Output |
34	|----------|-------|------------------|
35	| Zero entries | `count == 0` | Icon + "Comece a registrar..." |
36	| One entry | `count == 1` | 1 bar + "Ainda é cedo..." |
37	| >30 entries | `count > 30`, any `buckets.length` | Exactly 10 condensed bars, no text |
38	| Mid-range | `1 < count <= 30` | One bar per bucket, no text |
39	| Fetch fails | `Left(Failure)` | `ResourceError`, inline error text, no crash |
40	
41	</frozen-after-approval>
42	
43	## Code Map
44	
45	- `lib/features/dashboard/{data,domain,presentation}/` -- empty scaffold; all files below are new
46	- `lib/core/resource.dart:10-32` -- `Resource<T>`, `DashboardCubit`'s state type
47	- `entries_search_cubit.dart:20-21,140-170` -- emit/generation-guard template

60	- [x] `domain/entities/dashboard_aggregate.dart` -- `DashboardAggregate{totalCount, bucketCounts}` -- RNF06

## Intent

**Problem:** Configurações has no evolution chart yet; FR-09's "computed on demand, never stale" isn't met by anything in the codebase.

**Approach:** New `dashboard` feature (already scaffolded empty) fetches `GET /dashboard/aggregate` fresh on every Configurações open, and a new chart section renders one of several states by total entry count: 0 → placeholder, 1 → single bar, >30 → condensed to 10 bars. The narrative paragraph is out of scope (Story 8.2).

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Call `dashboard-aggregate-get` with `queryParameters: {'period': 'all'}` — fixed; no period selector exists anywhere in the product.
- `DashboardCubit` is a `registerLazySingleton` that constructor-subscribes to `PendingEntryWriteTracker.confirmedWrites`, recomputing on each event (entry created on another tab while this one stays mounted).
- `AccountSettingsScreen.initState` calls `dashboardCubit.load()` unconditionally (beside the existing `clearStaleError()`) so every open is a live fetch, never the singleton's stale state.
- States by `totals.count`: `0` → icon + "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui"; `1` → 1 bar + "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão..."; `>30` → `bucketCounts` left-padded with leading zeros to length 10 (when shorter) *before* condensing to exactly 10 bars via 10 contiguous index chunks, summed `count`, remainder in the last chunk, no text; `2..30` → one bar per bucket as-is, no text (matrix gap, resolved per AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed"). Bar height ∝ count / max count shown.
- `DashboardAggregateDto` mirrors the full contract (`buckets[].{date,count,sources}`, `totals.{count,sources}`, same precedent as `ExportJobStatusDto`); domain `DashboardAggregate` exposes only `totalCount`/`bucketCounts`.
- New visual tokens live only in `design_tokens.dart`, values read off `cerne-prototype.html`'s dashboard markup, reusing existing color/radius/elevation/spacing tokens wherever a pixel value already matches.

**Ask First:** None. **Never:** render the AI narrative, a period selector, or cache the aggregate (AD-15 exclusion).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input | Expected Output |
|----------|-------|------------------|
| Zero entries | `count == 0` | Icon + "Comece a registrar..." |
| One entry | `count == 1` | 1 bar + "Ainda é cedo..." |
| >30 entries | `count > 30`, any `buckets.length` | Exactly 10 condensed bars, no text |
| Mid-range | `1 < count <= 30` | One bar per bucket, no text |
| Fetch fails | `Left(Failure)` | `ResourceError`, inline error text, no crash |

9	/// "Sua evolução" — Story 8.1's own chart section on Configurações
10	/// (`cerne-prototype.html`'s Tela 6 dashboard block). Reads [DashboardCubit]
11	/// via `BlocBuilder` — `AccountSettingsScreen`'s own `MultiBlocProvider`
12	/// already makes it available higher up the tree, same convention
13	/// `MeusRegistrosScreen` already uses for its own two cubits.
14	///
15	/// The AI narrative paragraph is explicitly out of scope here (Story 8.2,
16	/// Intent/Never) — every branch below renders *at most* a short, hardcoded
17	/// Portuguese placeholder message, never anything derived from
18	/// `dashboard-narrative-get`.
19	class DashboardChartSection extends StatelessWidget {
20	  const DashboardChartSection({super.key});
21	
22	  static const _emptyMessage =
23	      'Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução '
24	      'aqui';
25	
26	  static const _oneEntryMessage =
27	      'Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte '
28	      'em alguns dias.';
29	
30	  /// Boundaries: "`buckets` condensed to exactly 10 bars".
31	  static const _targetCondensedBars = 10;
32	
33	  @override
34	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
35	    return Column(
36	      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
37	      children: [
38	        Text(
39	          'Sua evolução',
40	          style: DesignTokens.textHeadlineMd.copyWith(
41	            color: DesignTokens.colorTextPrimary,
42	          ),
43	        ),
44	        const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.dashboardSectionGap),
45	        BlocBuilder<DashboardCubit, Resource<DashboardAggregate>>(
46	          builder: (context, state) => _buildBody(state),
47	        ),
48	      ],
49	    );
50	  }
51	
52	  Widget _buildBody(Resource<DashboardAggregate> state) {
53	    return switch (state) {
54	      ResourceIdle<DashboardAggregate>() ||
55	      ResourceLoading<DashboardAggregate>() => _loadingCard(),
56	      ResourceError<DashboardAggregate>(failure: final failure) => _errorCard(
57	        failure.message,
58	      ),
59	      ResourceData<DashboardAggregate>(data: final aggregate) => _populatedCard(
60	        aggregate,
61	      ),
62	    };
63	  }
64	
65	  /// Review finding (round 2): uses [DesignTokens.dashboardCardPadding] —
66	  /// same padding [_populatedCard]'s own card uses — rather than
67	  /// [DesignTokens.spacingLg], so the card doesn't visibly resize on every
68	  /// loading -> data transition (including a background `confirmedWrites`
69	  /// refresh, which never shows this state to begin with but would have on
70	  /// a slow repeated `load()`).
71	  Widget _loadingCard() => _card(
72	    padding: const EdgeInsets.all(DesignTokens.dashboardCardPadding),
73	    child: const Center(
74	      child: CircularProgressIndicator(
75	        color: DesignTokens.colorAccent,
76	        semanticsLabel: 'Carregando gráfico de evolução',
77	      ),
78	    ),
79	  );
80	
81	  /// I/O matrix: "Fetch fails -> ResourceError, inline error text, no
82	  /// crash" — same inline-error treatment `AccountSettingsScreen`'s own
83	  /// biometric-toggle failure already uses ([DesignTokens.textBodyMd] +
84	  /// [DesignTokens.colorError]). Padding matches [_loadingCard]'s own
85	  /// review-fix rationale above.
86	  Widget _errorCard(String message) => _card(
87	    padding: const EdgeInsets.all(DesignTokens.dashboardCardPadding),
88	    child: Text(
89	      message,
90	      style: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorError),
91	    ),
92	  );
93	
94	  /// I/O matrix: "Zero entries -> icon + 'Comece a registrar...'".
95	  Widget _emptyCard() => _card(
96	    padding: const EdgeInsets.all(DesignTokens.spacingLg),
97	    child: Column(
98	      mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
99	      children: [
100	        // Review finding: a bare `Icon` with no `semanticLabel` is simply
101	        // excluded from the semantics tree (Flutter's own default) — a
102	        // screen-reader user hears nothing at all for it, relying entirely
103	        // on the text below. [_emptyMessage]'s own text already reads
104	        // naturally without the icon, so this label is purely additional
105	        // context, never a duplicate announcement of that same text.
106	        const Icon(
107	          Icons.show_chart,
108	          size: DesignTokens.dashboardEmptyStateIconSize,
109	          color: DesignTokens.colorBorder,
110	          semanticLabel: 'Gráfico de evolução vazio',
111	        ),
112	        const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.dashboardEmptyStateGap),
113	        Text(
114	          _emptyMessage,
115	          textAlign: TextAlign.center,
116	          style: DesignTokens.textLabelMd.copyWith(
117	            color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary,
118	          ),
119	        ),
120	      ],
121	    ),
122	  );
123	
124	  /// Boundaries' own count matrix: `0` is [_emptyCard]; `1` is exactly one
125	  /// full-height bar plus [_oneEntryMessage]; `>30` condenses
126	  /// [DashboardAggregate.bucketCounts] to exactly [_targetCondensedBars]
127	  /// bars via [_condense]; `2..30` renders one bar per bucket as-is — the
128	  /// "matrix gap" the frozen spec's own Boundaries line resolves per
129	  /// AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed". None of the non-zero branches ever
130	  /// renders text other than the `1`-count message (Boundaries: "no text").
131	  Widget _populatedCard(DashboardAggregate aggregate) {
132	    final totalCount = aggregate.totalCount;
133	    if (totalCount == 0) {
134	      return _emptyCard();
135	    }
136	
137	    List<int> barCounts;
138	    String? message;
139	    if (totalCount == 1) {
140	      barCounts = const [1];
141	      message = _oneEntryMessage;
142	    } else if (totalCount > 30) {
143	      barCounts = _condense(aggregate.bucketCounts);
144	    } else {
145	      barCounts = aggregate.bucketCounts;
146	    }
147	
148	    var maxCount = barCounts.fold(0, (max, count) => count > max ? count : max);
149	
150	    // Review finding (defensive guard): `totalCount > 0` with every
151	    // `barCounts` entry at 0 (or the list empty) is contract-inconsistent
152	    // (`totals.count` and the sum of every `buckets[].count` should
153	    // always agree) but not impossible against malformed/inconsistent
154	    // backend data — falls back to a single bar for the whole
155	    // [totalCount] rather than silently rendering an invisible bar row
156	    // (RNF09: never a blank/broken-looking screen over bad data). Checked
157	    // via `maxCount == 0` rather than `barCounts.isEmpty` so it also
158	    // catches `_condense`'s output, which is never empty (always exactly
159	    // [_targetCondensedBars] entries) even when every summed chunk is 0.
160	    if (maxCount == 0) {
161	      barCounts = [totalCount];
162	      maxCount = totalCount;
163	    }
164	
165	    return _card(
166	      padding: const EdgeInsets.all(DesignTokens.dashboardCardPadding),
167	      child: Column(
168	        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
169	        mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
170	        children: [
171	          // Review finding: each bar is a bare, unlabeled `Container` —
172	          // wrapping the whole row in one summarizing `Semantics` label
173	          // (and excluding the individual bars from the semantics tree)
174	          // gives a screen-reader user one meaningful announcement
175	          // instead of N anonymous elements.
176	          Semantics(
177	            label:
178	                'Gráfico de evolução: $totalCount registros no período, '
179	                'em ${barCounts.length} barras.',
180	            child: ExcludeSemantics(
181	              child: SizedBox(
182	                height: DesignTokens.dashboardBarAreaHeight,
183	                child: Row(
184	                  spacing: DesignTokens.spacingSm,
185	                  crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.end,
186	                  children: [
187	                    for (final count in barCounts)
188	                      DashboardChartBar(
189	                        // Review finding: clamped here, matching
190	                        // `DashboardChartBar`'s own doc comment — a
191	                        // negative `count` (malformed backend data)
192	                        // would otherwise produce a negative height and
193	                        // crash the `Container` below.
194	                        heightFraction: (count / maxCount).clamp(0, 1),
195	                      ),
196	                  ],
197	                ),
198	              ),
199	            ),
200	          ),
201	          if (message != null) ...[
202	            const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.dashboardSectionGap),
203	            Text(
204	              message,
205	              style: DesignTokens.textLabelMd.copyWith(
206	                color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary,
207	              ),
208	            ),
209	          ],
210	        ],
211	      ),
212	    );
213	  }
214	
215	  /// Boundaries (amended, Spec Change Log): "`bucketCounts` left-padded
216	  /// with leading zero-count entries to length 10 (when shorter) *before*
217	  /// condensing... via 10 contiguous index chunks, summed `count`,
218	  /// remainder in the last chunk". The original, frozen wording degenerated
219	  /// whenever `bucketCounts.length < _targetCondensedBars`: the floor-
220	  /// division chunk size was `0`, so the first 9 chunks each summed an
221	  /// *empty* range (always `0`) and the 10th silently absorbed the entire
222	  /// total — 9 invisible bars + 1 giant one, defeating the chart for any
223	  /// user whose activity concentrates into fewer than 10 distinct backend
224	  /// buckets while still exceeding 30 entries. [_pad] below removes that
225	  /// degeneracy: once [bucketCounts] is at least [_targetCondensedBars]
226	  /// long (real data, or zero-padded), the same "first 9 chunks of
227	  /// `length ~/ 10`, 10th absorbs the remainder" chunking produces a
228	  /// non-degenerate spread — leading zero bars, then the real data at the
229	  /// end, for a short [bucketCounts]. Always exactly [_targetCondensedBars]
230	  /// ints out, regardless of `bucketCounts.length` (I/O matrix: "`>30`
231	  /// entries, any `buckets.length`").
232	  static List<int> _condense(List<int> bucketCounts) {
233	    final padded = _pad(bucketCounts);
234	    final chunkSize = padded.length ~/ _targetCondensedBars;
235	    final condensed = <int>[];
236	    var index = 0;
237	    for (var i = 0; i < _targetCondensedBars - 1; i++) {
238	      final end = index + chunkSize;
239	      condensed.add(_sum(padded, index, end));
240	      index = end;
241	    }
242	    condensed.add(_sum(padded, index, padded.length));
243	    return condensed;
244	  }
245	
246	  /// Left-pads [bucketCounts] with leading zero-count entries up to
247	  /// [_targetCondensedBars] — a no-op once [bucketCounts] already has at
248	  /// least that many entries (Boundaries: "when shorter").
249	  static List<int> _pad(List<int> bucketCounts) {
250	    if (bucketCounts.length >= _targetCondensedBars) {
251	      return bucketCounts;
252	    }
253	    return [
254	      ...List<int>.filled(_targetCondensedBars - bucketCounts.length, 0),
255	      ...bucketCounts,
256	    ];
257	  }
258	
259	  static int _sum(List<int> list, int start, int end) {
260	    var total = 0;
261	    for (var i = start; i < end; i++) {
262	      total += list[i];
263	    }
264	    return total;
265	  }
266	
267	  Widget _card({required EdgeInsets padding, required Widget child}) {
268	    return Container(
269	      padding: padding,
270	      decoration: const BoxDecoration(
271	        color: DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated,
272	        borderRadius: BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusMd)),
273	        boxShadow: DesignTokens.elevation1,
274	      ),
275	      child: child,
276	    );
277	  }
278	}
279	
280	/// One chart bar — a `cerne-prototype.html` `chartBars` entry
281	/// (`flex:1;background:#C98A3E;border-radius:4px 4px 0 0`). [heightFraction]
282	/// is `count / maxCount` for whichever bars [DashboardChartSection] is
283	/// currently showing (Boundaries: "Bar height ∝ count / max count shown"),
284	/// clamped to `[0, 1]` by its own caller.
285	class DashboardChartBar extends StatelessWidget {
286	  const DashboardChartBar({required this.heightFraction, super.key});
287	
288	  final double heightFraction;
289	
290	  @override
291	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
292	    return Expanded(
293	      child: Container(
294	        height: DesignTokens.dashboardBarAreaHeight * heightFraction,
295	        decoration: const BoxDecoration(
296	          color: DesignTokens.colorAccent,
297	          borderRadius: BorderRadius.only(
298	            topLeft: Radius.circular(DesignTokens.dashboardBarRadius),
299	            topRight: Radius.circular(DesignTokens.dashboardBarRadius),
300	          ),
301	        ),
302	      ),
303	    );
304	  }
305	}

18	/// `register*Feature()` call in `setupCoreDependencies()` has already run.

---
title: 'Story 8.2: Independent Narrative Text & Narrative-Unavailable State'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-07'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Configurações' "Sua evolução" chart (spec-8-1) never shows the AI narrative paragraph FR-39 requires alongside it, and has no distinct state for when only that narrative fails.

**Approach:** Add a second, independent fetch (`GET /dashboard/narrative`) with its own `Resource<String>` cubit. Render the resulting text below the chart only in the >30-entries state — the only scenario with a narrative in the prototype — with a dedicated "unavailable, tap to retry" message when just that fetch fails; the chart itself never degrades.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Call `dashboard-narrative-get` with `queryParameters: {'period': 'all'}` — same fixed value as `dashboard-aggregate-get` (spec-8-1 precedent).
- New `DashboardNarrativeCubit extends Cubit<Resource<String>>`, mirroring `DashboardCubit`'s exact shape: `registerLazySingleton`, constructor-subscribes to `PendingEntryWriteTracker.confirmedWrites` (recompute on every entry write, same as the aggregate), `load()` is generation-guarded.
- `AccountSettingsScreen.initState` calls `narrativeCubit.load()` unconditionally, alongside the existing `dashboardCubit.load()` — two independent fetches fired in parallel, neither awaiting the other.
- `DashboardChartSection` renders the narrative section *only* inside its existing `totalCount > 30` branch — confirmed by `prototype-extract.md` (lines 110-113) and the raw prototype's `cenarioDashboard` enum (`Zero registros`/`Uma entrada`/`Mais de 30`): the AI narrative exists only in the >30 scenario; the `0`/`1`-count branches keep their current hardcoded messages untouched, never fetching or showing narrative text.
- Narrative states inside that branch: `ResourceData<String>` → the text, styled with a new `DesignTokens.dashboardNarrativeTextStyle` (Karla 400 · 13/20, read off `cerne-prototype.html`'s dashboard narrative markup — no existing token matches) + `colorTextSecondary`; `ResourceError<String>` → "Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora" in the same style, plus a tappable "tentar novamente" in `colorAccent` that re-calls `narrativeCubit.load()` (verbatim prototype copy/behavior — `cerne-prototype.html`'s `retryNarrative`); `Idle`/`Loading` → render nothing, so the chart never waits on the narrative.
- `DashboardNarrativeDto` mirrors the full contract (`text`, `generatedAt`), same "decode everything, domain narrows" precedent as `DashboardAggregateDto`; `toDomain()` returns only `text` as a plain `String` (one field — no new entity).
- `DashboardRepository`/`DashboardRemoteDataSource`/`DashboardRepositoryImpl` each gain one new method (`getNarrative`) — same files, same thin-pass-through/decode-to-`malformedResponse` shape as `getAggregate`, not a parallel class.
- `AccountSettingsScreen` announces a narrative `ResourceError` via its existing `_announce`, same as the chart's own error announcement (accessibility precedent, spec-8-1 round 2).

**Ask First:** None. **Never:** couple the two `Resource`s into one state object; show narrative text or its error for `0`/`1`-count states; call `dashboard-narrative-get` from anywhere but `DashboardNarrativeCubit.load()`.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| >30 entries, narrative resolves | aggregate `>30`, narrative `Right(text)` | Chart + narrative text below it | N/A |
| >30 entries, narrative fails | aggregate `>30`, narrative `Left(Failure)` | Chart renders normally; "Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora" + "tentar novamente" | Tap re-calls `load()`, no crash |
| 0 or 1 entries | aggregate count `0`/`1` | Narrative fetch result never rendered; existing hardcoded messages unchanged | N/A |
| Narrative fetch pending | `Idle`/`Loading` | No narrative section shown | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/dashboard/domain/repositories/dashboard_repository.dart:10-22` -- add `getNarrative({required period})` beside `getAggregate`
- `lib/features/dashboard/data/datasources/dashboard_remote_data_source.dart:12-33` -- add `getNarrative`, same `.get('dashboard-narrative-get', queryParameters:)` + try/catch-to-`malformedResponse` shape as `getAggregate`
- `lib/features/dashboard/data/repositories/dashboard_repository_impl.dart:13-25` -- add thin pass-through `getNarrative`
- new `lib/features/dashboard/data/models/dashboard_narrative_dto.dart` (+ `.g.dart`) -- `@JsonSerializable()`, fields `text`/`generatedAt`, `toDomain() => text`; mirror `dashboard_aggregate_dto.dart:1-31`'s structure
- `lib/features/dashboard/presentation/cubit/dashboard_cubit.dart:25-68` -- template for new `presentation/cubit/dashboard_narrative_cubit.dart` (`Cubit<Resource<String>>`, same constructor/`load()`/generation-guard/`confirmedWrites` shape)
- `lib/features/dashboard/dashboard_injection.dart:21-45` -- register `DashboardNarrativeCubit` as a second `registerLazySingleton`, same dependencies as `DashboardCubit`
- `lib/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/dashboard_chart_section.dart:131-213` (`_populatedCard`) -- thread `BuildContext` in, add a narrative `BlocBuilder<DashboardNarrativeCubit, Resource<String>>` only inside the `totalCount > 30` branch
- `lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart:17-30,45-48,65-76,183-193` -- add `narrativeCubit` constructor param, provide it, call `.load()` in `initState`, add a `BlocListener` announcing its `ResourceError`
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart:135-140` -- pass `sl<DashboardNarrativeCubit>()` to `AccountSettingsScreen`
- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart:780-807` -- append `dashboardNarrativeTextStyle` (Karla 400 · 13/20) beside the other dashboard tokens
- `test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen_test.dart:86-139` -- `_FakeDashboardRepository` needs a `getNarrative` override once the interface grows; add a `_buildNarrativeCubit` helper mirroring `_buildDashboardCubit`
- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1689-1736` -- `GET /dashboard/narrative` contract (frozen)
- `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md:110,113` + raw `cerne-prototype.html`'s `retryNarrative`/`narrativeFailed` logic -- source of the >30-only scoping and the retry-link behavior

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `dashboard_repository.dart` / `dashboard_remote_data_source.dart` / `dashboard_repository_impl.dart` -- add `getNarrative` -- new backend call, same layering as `getAggregate`
- [ ] `dashboard_narrative_dto.dart` (+ `.g.dart`) -- full-contract DTO + `toDomain()` -- DTO convention (RNF09)
- [ ] `dashboard_narrative_cubit.dart` -- `Cubit<Resource<String>>`, `load()` + generation guard + `confirmedWrites` subscription -- mirrors `DashboardCubit`
- [ ] `dashboard_injection.dart` -- register `DashboardNarrativeCubit` -- DI wiring
- [ ] `dashboard_chart_section.dart` -- render narrative text/error/retry inside the `>30` branch only -- I/O matrix
- [ ] `account_settings_screen.dart` + `app_router.dart` -- wire the new cubit through, `load()` on open, announce errors -- screen integration

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Configurações' "Sua evolução" chart (spec-8-1) never shows the AI narrative paragraph FR-39 requires alongside it, and has no distinct state for when only that narrative fails.

**Approach:** Add a second, independent fetch (`GET /dashboard/narrative`) with its own `Resource<String>` cubit. Render the resulting text below the chart only in the >30-entries state — the only scenario with a narrative in the prototype — with a dedicated "unavailable, tap to retry" message when just that fetch fails; the chart itself never degrades.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Call `dashboard-narrative-get` with `queryParameters: {'period': 'all'}` — same fixed value as `dashboard-aggregate-get` (spec-8-1 precedent).

- `AccountSettingsScreen.initState` calls `narrativeCubit.load()` unconditionally, alongside the existing `dashboardCubit.load()` — two independent fetches fired in parallel, neither awaiting the other.
- `DashboardChartSection` renders the narrative section *only* inside its existing `totalCount > 30` branch — confirmed by `prototype-extract.md` (lines 110-113) and the raw prototype's `cenarioDashboard` enum (`Zero registros`/`Uma entrada`/`Mais de 30`): the AI narrative exists only in the >30 scenario; the `0`/`1`-count branches keep their current hardcoded messages untouched, never fetching or showing narrative text.
- Narrative states inside that branch: `ResourceData<String>` → the text, styled with a new `DesignTokens.dashboardNarrativeTextStyle` (Karla 400 · 13/20, read off `cerne-prototype.html`'s dashboard narrative markup — no existing token matches) + `colorTextSecondary`; `ResourceError<String>` → "Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora" in the same style, plus a tappable "tentar novamente" in `colorAccent` that re-calls `narrativeCubit.load()` (verbatim prototype copy/behavior — `cerne-prototype.html`'s `retryNarrative`); `Idle`/`Loading` → render nothing, so the chart never waits on the narrative.
- `DashboardNarrativeDto` mirrors the full contract (`text`, `generatedAt`), same "decode everything, domain narrows" precedent as `DashboardAggregateDto`; `toDomain()` returns only `text` as a plain `String` (one field — no new entity).
- `DashboardRepository`/`DashboardRemoteDataSource`/`DashboardRepositoryImpl` each gain one new method (`getNarrative`) — same files, same thin-pass-through/decode-to-`malformedResponse` shape as `getAggregate`, not a parallel class.
- `AccountSettingsScreen` announces a narrative `ResourceError` via its existing `_announce`, same as the chart's own error announcement (accessibility precedent, spec-8-1 round 2).

**Ask First:** None. **Never:** couple the two `Resource`s into one state object; show narrative text or its error for `0`/`1`-count states; call `dashboard-narrative-get` from anywhere but `DashboardNarrativeCubit.load()`.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| >30 entries, narrative resolves | aggregate `>30`, narrative `Right(text)` | Chart + narrative text below it | N/A |
| >30 entries, narrative fails | aggregate `>30`, narrative `Left(Failure)` | Chart renders normally; "Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora" + "tentar novamente" | Tap re-calls `load()`, no crash |
| 0 or 1 entries | aggregate count `0`/`1` | Narrative fetch result never rendered; existing hardcoded messages unchanged | N/A |
| Narrative fetch pending | `Idle`/`Loading` | No narrative section shown | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/dashboard/domain/repositories/dashboard_repository.dart:10-22` -- add `getNarrative({required period})` beside `getAggregate`
- `lib/features/dashboard/data/datasources/dashboard_remote_data_source.dart:12-33` -- add `getNarrative`, same `.get('dashboard-narrative-get', queryParameters:)` + try/catch-to-`malformedResponse` shape as `getAggregate`

- new `lib/features/dashboard/data/models/dashboard_narrative_dto.dart` (+ `.g.dart`) -- `@JsonSerializable()`, fields `text`/`generatedAt`, `toDomain() => text`; mirror `dashboard_aggregate_dto.dart:1-31`'s structure
- `lib/features/dashboard/presentation/cubit/dashboard_cubit.dart:25-68` -- template for new `presentation/cubit/dashboard_narrative_cubit.dart` (`Cubit<Resource<String>>`, same constructor/`load()`/generation-guard/`confirmedWrites` shape)
- `lib/features/dashboard/dashboard_injection.dart:21-45` -- register `DashboardNarrativeCubit` as a second `registerLazySingleton`, same dependencies as `DashboardCubit`
- `lib/features/dashboard/presentation/widgets/dashboard_chart_section.dart:131-213` (`_populatedCard`) -- thread `BuildContext` in, add a narrative `BlocBuilder<DashboardNarrativeCubit, Resource<String>>` only inside the `totalCount > 30` branch
- `lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart:17-30,45-48,65-76,183-193` -- add `narrativeCubit` constructor param, provide it, call `.load()` in `initState`, add a `BlocListener` announcing its `ResourceError`
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart:135-140` -- pass `sl<DashboardNarrativeCubit>()` to `AccountSettingsScreen`

- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1689-1736` -- `GET /dashboard/narrative` contract (frozen)
- `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md:110,113` + raw `cerne-prototype.html`'s `retryNarrative`/`narrativeFailed` logic -- source of the >30-only scoping and the retry-link behavior

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `dashboard_repository.dart` / `dashboard_remote_data_source.dart` / `dashboard_repository_impl.dart` -- add `getNarrative` -- new backend call, same layering as `getAggregate`
- [ ] `dashboard_narrative_dto.dart` (+ `.g.dart`) -- full-contract DTO + `toDomain()` -- DTO convention (RNF09)
- [ ] `dashboard_narrative_cubit.dart` -- `Cubit<Resource<String>>`, `load()` + generation guard + `confirmedWrites` subscription -- mirrors `DashboardCubit`
- [ ] `dashboard_injection.dart` -- register `DashboardNarrativeCubit` -- DI wiring
- [ ] `dashboard_chart_section.dart` -- render narrative text/error/retry inside the `>30` branch only -- I/O matrix
- [ ] `account_settings_screen.dart` + `app_router.dart` -- wire the new cubit through, `load()` on open, announce errors -- screen integration
- [ ] `design_tokens.dart` -- `dashboardNarrativeTextStyle` -- AGENTS.md token rule
- [ ] Tests under `test/features/dashboard/` (datasource/repository/DTO/cubit/widget) covering the I/O matrix + retry tap + `confirmedWrites` recompute
- [ ] Update `account_settings_screen_test.dart`'s fake repository + helpers for the widened constructor

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the aggregate shows `totalCount > 30` and the narrative fetch resolves, when the screen renders, then the narrative text appears below the chart.
- Given the aggregate shows `totalCount > 30` and the narrative fetch fails, when the screen renders, then the chart still renders normally and a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message with a working retry shows — never blank, never the 0/1-entry wording.
- Given `totalCount` is `0` or `1`, when the screen renders, then no narrative text, error, or retry ever appears, regardless of the narrative fetch's own result.

## Spec Change Log

## Design Notes

The >30-only scoping isn't stated verbatim in `epics.md`'s AC text ("Given the chart has rendered with data") but is unambiguous once cross-referenced: `prototype-extract.md:110-113` gives the AI narrative only to "mais de 30 registros," gives "uma entrada" its own non-AI hardcoded line (already shipped verbatim in spec-8-1), and gives "zero entradas" explicitly "no summary paragraph" — and the raw prototype's `cenarioDashboard` enum itself has only three options, with `narrativeFailed` forcibly set to the `'Mais de 30'` scenario. Firing `narrativeCubit.load()` unconditionally (rather than gating the call on the aggregate's count) keeps the two fetches genuinely decoupled per Boundaries, at the cost of one harmless extra backend call for 0/1-count users whose result is simply never rendered.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` -- expected: `dashboard_narrative_dto.g.dart` generated, no conflicts
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test test/features/dashboard test/features/account` -- expected: all pass

**Manual checks (if no CLI):**
- Open Configurações against a >30-entry fixture with narrative success, narrative failure (+ retry tap), and 0/1-entry fixtures confirming no narrative UI appears — covered by widget tests in lieu of a device/simulator (AGENTS.md: none exists yet).

## Intent

**Problem:** Configurações' "Sua evolução" chart (spec-8-1) never shows the AI narrative paragraph FR-39 requires alongside it, and has no distinct state for when only that narrative fails.

**Approach:** Add a second, independent fetch (`GET /dashboard/narrative`) with its own `Resource<String>` cubit. ## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Call `dashboard-narrative-get` with `queryParameters: {'period': 'all'}` — same fixed value as `dashboard-aggregate-get` (spec-8-1 precedent).

- `AccountSettingsScreen.initState` calls `narrativeCubit.load()` unconditionally, alongside the existing `dashboardCubit.load()` — two independent fetches fired in parallel, neither awaiting the other.
- `DashboardChartSection` renders the narrative section *only* inside its existing `totalCount > 30` branch — confirmed by `prototype-extract.md` (lines 110-113) and the raw prototype's `cenarioDashboard` enum (`Zero registros`/`Uma entrada`/`Mais de 30`): the AI narrative exists only in the >30 scenario; the `0`/`1`-count branches keep their current hardcoded messages untouched, never fetching or showing narrative text.
- Narrative states inside that branch: `ResourceData<String>` → the text, styled with a new `DesignTokens.dashboardNarrativeTextStyle` (Karla 400 · 13/20, read off `cerne-prototype.html`'s dashboard narrative markup — no existing token matches) + `colorTextSecondary`; `ResourceError<String>` → "Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora" in the same style, plus a tappable "tentar novamente" in `colorAccent` that re-calls `narrativeCubit.load()` (verbatim prototype copy/behavior — `cerne-prototype.html`'s `retryNarrative`); `Idle`/`Loading` → render nothing, so the chart never waits on the narrative.
- `DashboardNarrativeDto` mirrors the full contract (`text`, `generatedAt`), same "decode everything, domain narrows" precedent as `DashboardAggregateDto`; `toDomain()` returns only `text` as a plain `String` (one field — no new entity).
- `DashboardRepository`/`DashboardRemoteDataSource`/`DashboardRepositoryImpl` each gain one new method (`getNarrative`) — same files, same thin-pass-through/decode-to-`malformedResponse` shape as `getAggregate`, not a parallel class.
- `AccountSettingsScreen` announces a narrative `ResourceError` via its existing `_announce`, same as the chart's own error announcement (accessibility precedent, spec-8-1 round 2).

**Ask First:** None. **Never:** couple the two `Resource`s into one state object; show narrative text or its error for `0`/`1`-count states; call `dashboard-narrative-get` from anywhere but `DashboardNarrativeCubit.load()`.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| >30 entries, narrative resolves | aggregate `>30`, narrative `Right(text)` | Chart + narrative text below it | N/A |
| >30 entries, narrative fails | aggregate `>30`, narrative `Left(Failure)` | Chart renders normally; "Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora" + "tentar novamente" | Tap re-calls `load()`, no crash |
| 0 or 1 entries | aggregate count `0`/`1` | Narrative fetch result never rendered; existing hardcoded messages unchanged | N/A |
| Narrative fetch pending | `Idle`/`Loading` | No narrative section shown | N/A |

2. Find the `development_status` entry matching `{story_key}`. If not found, warn the user once (`"{story_key} not found in sprint-status; skipping sprint sync"`) and return to caller.

4. Set `development_status[{story_key}]` to `{target_status}`.

7. Save the file, preserving ALL comments and structure including STATUS DEFINITIONS and WORKFLOW NOTES.

1	---
2	title: 'Story 8.2: Independent Narrative Text & Narrative-Unavailable State'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-11-07'
5	status: 'done'
6	review_loop_iteration: 0
7	context: []
8	baseline_commit: '6548fec2d856ea7063bb16f7e53d1745784c3eb2'
9	---
10	
11	<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
12	
13	## Intent
14	
15	**Problem:** Configurações' "Sua evolução" chart (spec-8-1) never shows the AI narrative paragraph FR-39 requires alongside it, and has no distinct state for when only that narrative fails.
16	
17	**Approach:** Add a second, independent fetch (`GET /dashboard/narrative`) with its own `Resource<String>` cubit. Render the resulting text below the chart only in the >30-entries state — the only scenario with a narrative in the prototype — with a dedicated "unavailable, tap to retry" message when just that fetch fails; the chart itself never degrades.
18	
19	## Boundaries & Constraints
20	
21	**Always:**
22	- Call `dashboard-narrative-get` with `queryParameters: {'period': 'all'}` — same fixed value as `dashboard-aggregate-get` (spec-8-1 precedent).
23	- New `DashboardNarrativeCubit extends Cubit<Resource<String>>`, mirroring `DashboardCubit`'s exact shape: `registerLazySingleton`, constructor-subscribes to `PendingEntryWriteTracker.confirmedWrites` (recompute on every entry write, same as the aggregate), `load()` is generation-guarded.
24	- `AccountSettingsScreen.initState` calls `narrativeCubit.load()` unconditionally, alongside the existing `dashboardCubit.load()` — two independent fetches fired in parallel, neither awaiting the other.
25	- `DashboardChartSection` renders the narrative section *only* inside its existing `totalCount > 30` branch — confirmed by `prototype-extract.md` (lines 110-113) and the raw prototype's `cenarioDashboard` enum (`Zero registros`/`Uma entrada`/`Mais de 30`): the AI narrative exists only in the >30 scenario; the `0`/`1`-count branches keep their current hardcoded messages untouched, never fetching or showing narrative text.
26	- Narrative states inside that branch: `ResourceData<String>` → the text, styled with a new `DesignTokens.dashboardNarrativeTextStyle` (Karla 400 · 13/20, read off `cerne-prototype.html`'s dashboard narrative markup — no existing token matches) + `colorTextSecondary`; `ResourceError<String>` → "Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora" in the same style, plus a tappable "tentar novamente" in `colorAccent` that re-calls `narrativeCubit.load()` (verbatim prototype copy/behavior — `cerne-prototype.html`'s `retryNarrative`); `Idle`/`Loading` → render nothing, so the chart never waits on the narrative.
27	- `DashboardNarrativeDto` mirrors the full contract (`text`, `generatedAt`), same "decode everything, domain narrows" precedent as `DashboardAggregateDto`; `toDomain()` returns only `text` as a plain `String` (one field — no new entity).
28	- `DashboardRepository`/`DashboardRemoteDataSource`/`DashboardRepositoryImpl` each gain one new method (`getNarrative`) — same files, same thin-pass-through/decode-to-`malformedResponse` shape as `getAggregate`, not a parallel class.
29	- `AccountSettingsScreen` announces a narrative `ResourceError` via its existing `_announce`, same as the chart's own error announcement (accessibility precedent, spec-8-1 round 2).
30	
31	**Ask First:** None. **Never:** couple the two `Resource`s into one state object; show narrative text or its error for `0`/`1`-count states; call `dashboard-narrative-get` from anywhere but `DashboardNarrativeCubit.load()`.
32	
33	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
34	
35	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
36	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
37	| >30 entries, narrative resolves | aggregate `>30`, narrative `Right(text)` | Chart + narrative text below it | N/A |
38	| >30 entries, narrative fails | aggregate `>30`, narrative `Left(Failure)` | Chart renders normally; "Não foi possível gerar o balanço agora" + "tentar novamente" | Tap re-calls `load()`, no crash |
39	| 0 or 1 entries | aggregate count `0`/`1` | Narrative fetch result never rendered; existing hardcoded messages unchanged | N/A |
40	| Narrative fetch pending | `Idle`/`Loading` | No narrative section shown | N/A |
